label: Yambuku
sub: 1976 index site — 318 cases, 280 deaths. First Ebola outbreak ever recorded. Zaire ebolavirus.

label: Nzara, South Sudan
sub: 1976 Sudan strain outbreak — 284 cases, 151 deaths. CFR 53%. Cotton factory workers.

label: Kikwit
sub: 1995 EBOV outbreak — 315 cases, 250 deaths. Amplified in Kikwit General Hospital.

label: Gulu, Uganda
sub: 2000–01 Sudan ebolavirus — 425 cases, 224 deaths. Largest SUDV outbreak on record.

label: Bundibugyo, Uganda
sub: 2007 BDBV discovery — 149 cases, 37 deaths. First identification of Bundibugyo species.

label: Isiro, DRC
sub: 2012 Bundibugyo strain — 77 cases, 36 deaths. Second and most recent BDBV outbreak before 2026.

label: Guéckédou, Guinea
sub: 2013 West Africa epidemic index case — Emile Ouamouno (18 months), deceased 6 Dec 2013.

label: Conakry, Guinea
sub: 2014 major transmission hub — capital city seeding with early West Africa epidemic

label: Monrovia, Liberia
sub: 2014 epicenter — health system collapsed Sep 2014. ELWA3 ETU overwhelmed. 4,809 deaths in Liberia.

label: Freetown, Sierra Leone
sub: 2014 epicenter — Sierra Leone reported 14,122 cases, highest national count in West Africa epidemic.

label: Beni, DRC
sub: 2018–2020 Kivu outbreak epicenter — ADF militia attacks on ETU hampered response. 3,481 cases total.

label: Butembo, DRC
sub: 2018–2020 Kivu major cluster — ETU attacked multiple times. Strong community resistance to response.

label: Goma, DRC
sub: 2019 PHEIC trigger — first Kivu case in 1M-person lake city with intl airport. Prompted WHO PHEIC July 2019.

label: Mahagi Territory, Ituri
sub: 2026 BDBV index cluster — Dec 2025 initial detection. Bushmeat hunting spillover. Active transmission zone.

label: Djugu Territory
sub: Active 2026 outbreak zone — Ituri Province spans 17 health zones with 341 confirmed cases as of June 3. Access restricted by armed group activity in ~23% of zone.

label: Irumu Territory
sub: Active 2026 outbreak zone — 31 cases. ETU operational as of March 2026.

label: Bundibugyo District, Uganda
sub: Active 2026 cross-border cases — 3 confirmed Feb 2026. Contact tracing 87 exposed persons.

label: Kinshasa
sub: DRC national EOC + MoH coordination hub. WHO AFRO regional office. Vaccine cold-chain distribution center.

label: Kampala, Uganda
sub: Uganda MoH national EOC. WHO Uganda Country Office. Border screening coordination.

label: Bunia ETU
sub: Ebola Treatment Unit — Bunia, Ituri capital. 40-bed capacity. MSF-supported. Active since Feb 2026.

label: Mahagi ETU
sub: Field ETU — 20-bed capacity deployed by DRC MoH/MSF. First patients admitted Jan 2026.

label: Kasese District, Uganda
sub: Quarantine zone — 23 contacts under monitoring as of May 2026. Uganda MoH isolation facility.

label: Mpondwe-Kasindi Border Crossing
sub: DRC-Uganda border checkpoint — enhanced screening since Feb 2026. WHO point-of-entry team deployed.

label: Arua, Uganda
sub: Regional CDC/WHO supply hub for northern Uganda response. Vaccine cold storage.

label: Dakar, Senegal
sub: WHO AFRO Emergency Hub and GOARN coordination node for West/Central Africa outbreak response.

label: Goma / Nord-Kivu, DRC
sub: 2026 outbreak expansion — confirmed BDBV cases in Nord-Kivu province including Goma by ~May 19. High population density and cross-border movement with Rwanda elevated risk. WHO DRC risk raised to Very High.

label: Bukavu / Sud-Kivu, DRC
sub: First South Kivu case confirmed 21 May 2026 — third DRC province affected. Patient died near Bukavu with travel history to Nord-Kivu, indicating spread via displacement corridors.

label: Kampala + Wakiso, Uganda (15 Lab-Confirmed / Local Transmission)
sub: 2026 BDBV cases in Uganda — 15 lab-confirmed as of 3 June (8 Kampala + 1 Wakiso district). 7 cases from local transmission chains; 4 with DRC travel links. 147+ contacts under 21-day monitoring. Uganda DRC border closed 4 weeks from 28 May (day 8).

label: Mongbwalu, Ituri
sub: 322 suspected cases, 88 deaths — largest cluster in outbreak. ETU fire May 23, four attack waves May 24–26; 25+ patients at large. MSF operations suspended May 26 pending security guarantees.

label: MSF Goma ETC (80-bed)
sub: MSF 80-bed Ebola Treatment Centre opened 1 June 2026 in Goma, Nord-Kivu — first patients admitted. Largest ETC established in the 2026 outbreak to date. Addresses 15 confirmed Nord-Kivu cases as of June 1.

label: MSF Bukavu ETC (under construction)
sub: MSF ETC under construction in Bukavu, Sud-Kivu as of 1 June 2026. One of two South Kivu ETCs (other: Lwiro). Responds to 3 confirmed BDBV cases in Sud-Kivu province.

label: MSF Mongbwalu ETC (65-bed, under construction)
sub: MSF 65-bed Ebola Treatment Centre under construction in Mongbwalu, Ituri as of 2 June 2026. Addresses the outbreak's largest and most volatile cluster zone — Mongbwalu had 322 suspected cases and 88 deaths with ongoing community resistance. Complements the Bunia ETU (40-bed) and Goma ETC (80-bed, operational June 1).

label: Rwampara, Ituri
sub: ETU torched 21 May 2026 by protesters objecting to safe-burial protocol. Tents destroyed, 6 patients transferred to Bunia hospital. Represents ongoing community resistance to response.

label: Mambasa Territory (IS-Controlled — No Access)
sub: Confirmed Ebola cases as of 6 June 2026 in Mambasa Territory, Ituri — controlled by Islamic State-affiliated armed groups. Health workers cannot enter; contact tracing, isolation, and ETU referral all impossible. Complete access denial zone within the outbreak footprint.

label: Kampala + Wakiso, Uganda (19 Confirmed — 2 Deaths)
sub: 2026 BDBV cases in Uganda — 19 lab-confirmed as of 5 June (8 Kampala + 1 Wakiso + new contact-linked). 2 confirmed deaths (first Uganda fatalities beyond index). 668+ contacts under 21-day monitoring. Uganda DRC border closed (May 28, 4-week closure, in second week).

label: Buta, Bas-Uélé Province (6th Province)
sub: Sixth DRC province affected — a motorcycle-taxi driver died 13 August 2026 in Buta after traveling from Isiro, Haut-Uélé. Bas-Uélé borders Central African Republic conflict-displacement corridors; poor roads and limited communications complicate response.

label: Mutwanga, North Kivu
sub: Newly confirmed health zone as of WHO Situation Report #15 (23 August 2026) — one of two new health zones (alongside Viadana, Bas-Uélé) added since the 18 August report, bringing the total to 57 affected health zones across six provinces. Located on the western slopes of the Rwenzori Mountains near the Uganda border.
